name: Sinking of Moskva Flagship
detail: On April 13–14, 2022, Ukraine struck and sank the Moskva — flagship of Russia's Black Sea Fleet — using two domestically-developed Neptune anti-ship cruise missiles. The Moskva sank while being towed, with an estimated 27–40 crew killed and 100+ missing. It was Russia's worst naval loss since the Falklands War and a massive psychological blow, undermining Russia's control of the western Black Sea.

name: Kerch Bridge Truck Bomb
detail: On October 8, 2022, a massive truck bomb detonated on the Kerch Bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea, collapsing two road spans and igniting fuel tanker cars. The attack was attributed to Ukraine's Security Service (SBU). Putin had personally inaugurated the bridge in 2018. A second Ukrainian strike in July 2023 using Storm Shadow missiles caused additional damage. The bridge remained a critical supply route throughout the war.

name: HIMARS Strike Campaign — Russian Ammo Depots
detail: Starting June 2022, Ukraine systematically used HIMARS to destroy 30+ Russian ammunition depots in a matter of months. Key strikes included depots in Nova Kakhovka, Chornobaivka, Kherson Oblast. The campaign forced Russia to move ammunition 80+ km from the front, dramatically degrading Russian artillery rates. ISW credited this campaign as a major factor in enabling Ukraine's Kherson counteroffensive.

name: Attacks on Black Sea Fleet Headquarters
detail: Ukraine repeatedly struck Russia's Black Sea Fleet headquarters in Sevastopol, Crimea through 2023–2024. The most significant attack came September 22, 2023 — a Storm Shadow missile strike on the fleet headquarters that killed the fleet's deputy commander and caused major damage. By mid-2024, Russia had relocated much of its Black Sea Fleet from Sevastopol to Novorossiysk on the Russian mainland, essentially ceding Crimea's maritime security role.

name: Kursk Oblast Incursion — Russian Territory
detail: On August 6, 2024, Ukraine launched a surprise offensive into Russia's Kursk Oblast — the first time since WWII that a foreign military occupied Russian territory. Ukrainian forces captured over 1,300 km² at peak, including Sudzha (gas transit hub), and held portions of Kursk for 7+ months. Ukraine captured 594+ Russian POWs in the first weeks for potential exchange. The operation forced Russia to divert troops from Donbas.

name: Long-Range Drone Strikes on Russian Territory
detail: Starting 2023, Ukraine launched increasingly deep drone strikes into Russian territory — including oil refineries, air bases, and industrial facilities hundreds of kilometers inside Russia. Key strikes targeted: Engels-2 Strategic Aviation Base (twice, 2022–2023), Saratov and Ryazan refineries, Lipetsk air base, and the Moscow suburb of Zhukovsky (aircraft factory). Ukraine did not officially claim most attacks but they were attributed to Ukrainian intelligence/military.

name: Snake Island Liberated
detail: Ukraine retook Snake Island on June 30, 2022 after forcing Russian evacuation through sustained HIMARS, artillery, and drone strikes on the island's garrison. Russia had captured the island February 24, 2022 in the famous exchange where Ukrainian defenders reportedly told the Russian warship 'go fuck yourself.' Liberation denied Russia a strategic platform for Black Sea operations and was a major psychological victory.

name: ATACMS Strikes on Crimea Airfields
detail: After receiving ATACMS authorization in 2023–2024, Ukraine struck Russian military airfields in Crimea including Saki, Belbek, and Sarabuz. The October 2023 strike on Berdiansk port destroyed Russian naval landing ships. ATACMS strikes significantly reduced Russia's ability to use Crimea as a launching platform for air and naval operations and forced redistribution of Russian aircraft.

name: Neptune Missile Strike — Atlant Aero Drone Factory, Taganrog
detail: On April 19, 2026, Ukrainian Navy Neptune cruise missiles struck the Atlant Aero manufacturing plant in Taganrog, Rostov Oblast. Two production facilities were destroyed and four others damaged. The plant manufactures Molniya strike-reconnaissance UAVs and Orion drone components used in Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities. Confirmed by Ukrainian General Staff and satellite imagery analysis on April 24. At least the third strike on this specific facility (previous hits included January 2026). Russia's Defense Ministry claimed air defense intercepted a Neptune missile during the period.

name: SBU Drones Strike Gorky Oil Pumping Station — Nizhny Novgorod
detail: Overnight April 22-23, 2026, SBU Special Operations Center 'A' drones struck the Gorky oil pumping station (Transneft) in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, Russia. Three oil storage tanks were damaged and a fire spread across 20,000 square meters. The station is part of the Transneft pipeline system feeding the Lukoil refinery in Kstovo. Part of a coordinated wave of over 150 Ukrainian drones launched against Russia and occupied Crimea, continuing Ukraine's systematic campaign to degrade Russian oil export and processing infrastructure.

name: Ukraine Strikes Primorsk — Russia's Largest Baltic Crude Oil Export Terminal
detail: Overnight May 2–3, 2026, Ukrainian forces launched over 60 UAVs at Primorsk, Russia's largest Baltic crude oil export terminal in Leningrad Oblast — the endpoint of the Baltic Pipeline System with ~1 million barrels/day loading capacity. NASA satellites confirmed active fires at the terminal. The regional governor initially reported 35 drones shot down, with the total rising above 60 by dawn. The strike caused severe aviation disruption: 70+ flights delayed and ~24 canceled at St. Petersburg's Pulkovo Airport (restrictions lasted ~6 hours, aircraft diverted). OSINT analysts suggested a Russian Pantsir air defense system at the port was also hit. This was the second major strike on Primorsk following the March 2026 attacks, continuing Ukraine's campaign to cut ~40% of Russia's Baltic oil export capacity. Zelenskyy described Ukraine's energy infrastructure strikes as 'a new stage in the use of Ukrainian weapons to limit the potential of Russia's war machine.'

name: Ukraine Strikes Tuapse Oil Refinery (4th Time in 16 Days) + Shadow Fleet Tankers
detail: On May 3, 2026, Ukraine struck Rosneft's Tuapse oil refinery on the Black Sea coast for the fourth time in 16 days, while also hitting 2–3 'shadow fleet' tankers allegedly transporting Russian crude in violation of G7 price cap sanctions. Earlier April strikes on Tuapse had sparked fires severe enough to force local evacuations and caused 'black rain' (oily droplets) over the town with elevated benzene levels. The shadow fleet tankers targeted were allegedly engaged in sanctions evasion. The coordinated campaign against Tuapse and the tanker fleet represents a multi-pronged effort to cut Russian war funding through energy infrastructure and illicit sanctions-busting oil trade.

name: Ukrainian Drone Strikes Luxury Moscow High-Rise 6 km from Kremlin — 5 Days Before Victory Day
detail: On the night of May 3–4, 2026, a Ukrainian drone struck the 'Dom na Mosfilmovskoy' luxury residential complex on Mosfilmovskaya Street in Moscow — approximately 6 km from the Kremlin. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin confirmed 5 drones targeted the capital; 2 were downed before reaching the city, causing visible structural damage to the tower with no reported casualties. The strike came 5 days before Russia's Victory Day parade (May 9), which Russian authorities had already announced would not feature military vehicles for the first time in approximately 20 years. The attack is one of the deepest confirmed Ukrainian drone strikes into Moscow's residential core and was timed to maximize psychological impact ahead of Putin's showcase military ceremony. Ukraine did not publicly claim responsibility.

name: Ukraine Strikes Perm Lukoil Refinery for 3rd Time in 2 Weeks + Transneft Hub — 1,500 km Inside Russia
detail: On May 8, 2026 — while Russia's declared Victory Day ceasefire was nominally in effect — Ukraine's SBU 'Alpha' Special Operations Center launched drones against the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery and the Perm linear production dispatch station (a Transneft hub) in Perm, Ural region. Fires broke out at a crude distillation unit and a storage tank. This was the third strike on the Perm refinery in two weeks, demonstrating Ukraine's ability to sustain precision campaign pressure against individual high-value Russian industrial targets at extreme range. The facility is approximately 1,500 km from the Ukrainian border — among the deepest confirmed oil infrastructure strikes of the war. Confirmed by SBU official statement, Ukrinform, Kyiv Independent, and Kyiv Post.

name: Ukraine Strikes Russian Missile Ship in Caspian Sea — First Strike on Caspian Flotilla
detail: Overnight May 7–8, 2026, Ukrainian forces struck a Project 22800 Karakurt-class small missile ship at Russia's naval base in Kaspiysk, Dagestan — on the Caspian Sea approximately 1,800 km from Ukraine. This is believed to be the first confirmed Ukrainian strike on the Russian Caspian Flotilla. Karakurt-class vessels are armed with Kalibr cruise missiles capable of striking targets across Ukraine. The attack significantly extends Ukraine's capacity to threaten Russian naval assets, previously focused on the Black Sea Fleet. Ukraine did not officially claim the strike, but Kyiv-based open-source analysts attributed it to SBU Special Operations assets based on trajectory and platform consistency.

name: Operation 'Snow for Akhmat' — Ukraine Destroys Chechen Drone Pilot Academy in Snizhne; 65+ Killed
detail: On the night of May 20–21, 2026 (confirmed May 22), Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, coordinated with the SBU, executed Operation 'Snow for Akhmat.' Eleven drones armed with 100 kg warheads struck a 2,484 sq-meter Sever-Akhmat drone pilot training complex in Snizhne, Russian-occupied Donetsk Oblast. The facility housed Chechen (Akhmat) military cadets, drone assembly areas, explosives storage, and a command post. Ukraine reported 65 cadets killed along with their commanding officer, Lt. Col. 'Buryi' — a Ph.D. at Russia's Academy of Missile and Artillery Sciences — and approximately 1 instructor. Simultaneously, Ukrainian forces struck a Russian FSB headquarters and an air defense system. President Zelensky confirmed the combined operations killed and wounded nearly 100 Russian personnel. Confirmed by CNN, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, and Defense Express.

name: Ukraine Strikes Sheskharis Oil Terminal + Grushovaya Depot + Shadow Tanker — Novorossiysk, Russia's Largest Black Sea Crude Hub
detail: On May 23, 2026, Ukraine's General Staff confirmed long-range drone strikes on the Sheskharis oil terminal and Grushovaya oil depot at Novorossiysk — Russia's largest Black Sea crude oil export hub, handling approximately 75 million tons of crude per year (~20% of Russia's total crude exports). Fires broke out at both oil facilities; two people were wounded. A shadow-fleet tanker named 'Chrysalis' was also struck in the port. Novorossiysk is Russia's primary Black Sea chokepoint for crude oil exports, making it a critical target in Ukraine's sustained campaign to degrade Russia's energy revenue that funds the war. Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Fortune, and The Moscow Times confirmed the fires. The strike continues Ukraine's 2026 campaign against Russian energy export infrastructure — from Baltic ports (Ust-Luga, Primorsk) to Black Sea refineries (Tuapse, 4 strikes) and now Russia's largest Black Sea crude hub.

name: Ukraine Strikes 66 Russian Targets Overnight — Kombinat Kamenskiy Rocket-Fuel Plant, MiG-29, Ozon Warehouses
detail: On August 24, 2026, Ukrainian drones struck 66 targets across Russia and occupied territory overnight, commander Robert 'Madyar' Brovdi said. Targets included the Kombinat Kamenskiy defense-industrial plant in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, Rostov Oblast — which produces solid rocket fuel for Uragan, Smerch, and Tornado-S multiple-launch rocket systems — a MiG-29 fighter jet near Dolotinka, three Ozon logistics warehouses in Dagestan, Stavropol Krai, and Adygea (Ozon shares fell 12%), four radar systems, a SOBR special police base in occupied Strilkove (Kherson Oblast), energy facilities in occupied Ukrainian territory, and two Russian 'shadow fleet' vessels in the Black Sea. It followed an August 23 strike reportedly hitting an Ozon warehouse in Orenburg, ~1,000km from the border. Debris from an intercepted Ukrainian drone struck a childcare center in Krasnodar, killing 2 children and injuring 9, per Russian officials — underscoring the campaign's growing reach and cost.
